cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Ewe strip-woven hammock (kete-style narrow-strip weaving with supplementary weft motifs, animals, objects, inscriptions, and tasseled fringe), a well-documented Ewe/Ghanaian textile tradition.

physical.title: hammock
physical.summary: Hammock composed of hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton hand-sewn together along the selvedges; there are eight strips with extensive decoration, and two along the edges that have minimal decoration. The hammock is two-sided, with the cloth folded to give two different panels on either side with different designs. The monochrome ground weave on both sides is plain woven with orange/brown in both warp and weft. There is extensive decoration formed by blocks of coloured weft using a second pair of heddles that block out the ground weave; between these are areas of with patterns woven in discontinuous supplementary weft using yarn coloured in light and dark green, orange, yellow, red, black, purple and blue. These patterns consist of geometric patterns and representations of animals. Along the centre of the hammock on the upper side is woven the text "Walter Bell Rest A While" in supplementary weft. Along the edges of the warp are tassels made from yellow, orange, purple, red, green, blue, grey and white cotton. At the ends of the hammock, the warps have been plaited together and wrapped in coloured cotton in order to attach carrying poles to the hammock.

cultural.vision_reason: A multi-strip narrow-loom cotton cloth with complex warp stripes and weft-faced supplementary blocks, a classic Ewe kente-type man's wrap cloth from Ghana, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary: Ewe cloth; man's wrap-around garment with cotton warp and weft. Composed of 21 narrow strips handsewn together in black cotton, selvedge to selvedge. Each strip consists of repeating plain weave warp stripes in same combination of black-, blue-, white-, red-, green-, yellow-, and cream-dyed cotton. Each warp strip includes a 'tweed' effect stripe formed by twisting together yellow and blue threads into a single strand. Warp stripes alternate at fixed intervals with weft-faced blocks in red-, yellow-, pink-, white-, blue- and purple-dyed cotton. Discontinuous suppplementary weft motifs are interspersed between the warp stripes and weft blocks and include motifs such as animals, birds and human figures as well as fans, hearts, trees, tools and combs. The cloth has turned and hand-stitched hems at either end.

physical.title: garment; cloth
physical.summary:
Wrapper; hand-woven plain weave cotton cloth with supplementary weft in rayon thread. Composed of 21 narrow warp-faced strips machine-sewn together at the selvedges. Two alternating strips: blue and white cotton warp with black cotton and gold rayon weft; banded border at each end with continuous supplementary weft patterns in blue and gold rayon. Red cotton warp and weft; banded border at each end with supplementary weft in gold rayon. Unworked warp fringe on all strips.

Main design elements worked in discontinuous supplementary weft in multi-coloured rayon thread. Designs include: diamond, chameleon, bird, sword, key, quadruped, butterfly. These mainly representational motifs are set within a larger diamond formed from 24 rectangles arranged in stepped pattern across the strips. Rectangles are worked in discontinuous supplementary weft: blue and gold rayon on the red strips; burgundy and gold rayon on the blue and white strips.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Ewe Keta cloth: a strip-woven cotton wrapper with warp-striped and weft-float block patterns in the colors and layout typical of southern Ghana/Togo Ewe weaving. It clearly matches a garment/textile made and worn by the Ewe.

physical.title: textile; wrapper
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 18 strips of hand-woven cotton, hand-sewn together along the selvages. All the cotton is industrial European thread of five colours: white, blue, red, green and yellow. There are two different warp patterns, which are arranged alternately across the cloth. The first pattern is warp-faced, and consists of  symmetrically arranged stripes of dark blue, white, red and yellow; the weft is of dark blue. The second pattern has a white warp through which run 12 narrow and two broad line of the dark blue. Its weft is of white cotton, interspersed at regular intervals by triple narrow stripes of blue; the main design is created by weaving two or three weft blocks per strip using a second pair of heddles; these are in a variety of sequences of line of red, black, green, blue and white. The warp ends have hand-sewn hems.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary: Ewe man's cloth, composed to 19 narrow strips of hand-spun cotton, hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The bottom side of the cloth is bordered by a narrower red band between two yellow bands. The warp is of cotton dyed yellow. The weft has bands of yellow and deep pink cotton of equal length, separated by a narrow stripe of pale blue. The yellow bands are themselves crossed by two stripes of blue bordered by white cotton. The 19 strips are aligned so that the pink and yellow squares form a chequerboard pattern. The dye is local, and no use is made of a second pair of heddles.

cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven strip-woven cotton wrapper (Keta cloth) with narrow-strip construction and weft-float geometric motifs is a classic Ewe textile form from the Volta Region of Ghana. This matches the claimed Ewe ethnicity well.

physical.title: wrapper; textile
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 20 strips of hand-woven cotton, hand-sewn together along the selvages, with a standard warp pattern but with varying weft float designs. All the cotton is industrial European thread of four colours: white, red, yellow and two shades of blue. The warp pattern uses a dark blue background with one stripe of light blue and six white lines. The weft-faced patterns use a second pair of heddles, and (with a few exceptions) a standard block composed of dark blue, white, red and yellow. These are usually placed as pairs, between which are discontinuous weft float motifs in yellow. The warp ends have been hand-sewn with a hem.

physical.title: textile; wrapper
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 12 strips of hand-woven cotton hand-sewn together along the selvages. All the cotton is industrial and imported from Europe. The warp design on all the strips is identical, being composed of alternating threads of yellow and dark blue with a wider central stripe of both colours. All the strips are crossed by weft blocks (using a second pair of heddles), which are arranged in two patterns that alternate across the cloth. The first pattern is of blocks of primarily yellow with some white and red; the second is primarily of red, with some black and yellow. The warp ends have not been hemmed.

physical.title: textile; wrapper
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 10 strips of hand-woven cotton hand-sewn together along the selvages, with two different warp patterns which are arranged alternately across the cloth. All the cotton is industrial European thread of three colours, white, blue and yellow. The first pattern has a warp of alternating pinstripe yellow and white threads, with a broad blue stripe along the centre which is interrupted by two narrow white lines; the weft is white, except for five regularly spaced bands of blue that create a ‘hidden’ pattern across the strip. The second pattern is of blue thread, divided by three narrow stripes of yellow; the weft is blue, except for three or four places where it is interrupted by lines of yellow. The warp ends have not been hemmed.
